B: Hi! Can you hear me? I genuinely thought the last one was the last one.
A: Ha. Yeah, me too. I can hear you. Darren.
B: Ollie. Nice to meet you. How's it been going?
A: Alright. Bit odd, talking to a laptop. What is it you do?
B: I'm a student, second year geography at King's in London. You?
A: Gas engineer. Boilers, central heating. Firm in Halesowen.
B: Oh, actually, can I ask you something about that? We had a lecture on heat pumps last term, decarbonising homes, and everyone in the room was like, yeah, just put heat pumps in everywhere. But nobody in the room had ever actually fitted one.
A: No, they wouldn't have.
B: So what's the real story?
A: Well. They work, in the right house. New build, good insulation, proper size radiators or underfloor, they're fine. Problem is most of what I go in is seventies, eighties semis, single skin in places, loft half done, little rads. You stick a heat pump on that and it runs all day and the house still isn't warm, and the customer's bill's gone up. So you've got to do the house first, and nobody's budgeting for that. That's where it falls down, really.
B: Right, so it's the fabric of the building more than the tech.
A: That's it. The tech's alright. Mostly.
B: That's really useful, honestly. That's the sort of thing that doesn't make it into the reading.
A: You'd want to talk to the lads doing the jobs, to be fair. Not the people selling them.
B: Noted. My dissertation's going to be on cycle lanes, so different thing, but same idea, like who it actually works for.
A: Cycle lanes. I'll be honest, they're a pain in the van.
B: Ha, everyone says that.
A: I've got kit in the back, I'm across four jobs a day. I can't do that on a bike.
B: No, totally. It's not really aimed at you. More people going two miles to the shops.
A: Fair enough. That I'd go along with.
B: Do you get out much outside work?
A: Walk the dog. Clent Hills, weekends. Bit of fishing.
B: Oh nice, I've heard Clent's good for running.
A: Hilly. Lot of runners up there, to be fair. You run?
B: Yeah, parkrun most Saturdays. Bit obsessed, honestly.
A: Bonnie'd chase you. Spaniel. She'd chase anything.
B: Ha, I've been chased by a fair few dogs at Burgess Park.
A: What's your Sunday look like, then? Bit of a lie-in?
B: Batch cooking. I do a chilli or pasta bake, Tupperware for the week. And every couple of weeks we do a house roast. My roast potatoes are, I'll be honest, quite good.
A: Goose fat?
B: Obviously.
A: Good lad. We go to my mum's every few weeks for Sunday dinner. She does—
